info.desc: Live Through This is the second studio album by American alternative rock band Hole, released on April 12, 1994, by DGC Records. Recorded in late 1993, it departed from the band's unpolished hardcore aesthetics to more refined melodies and song structure. Frontwoman Courtney Love said that she wanted the record to be "shocking to the people who think that we don't have a soft edge", but maintain a harsh sensibility. The album was produced by Sean Slade and Paul Q. Kolderie and mixed by Scott Litt and J Mascis. The lyrics and packaging reflect Love's thematic preoccupations with beauty, and .

podcast.body: Courtney Love and Hole had an earlier album and a high profile through her relationship with Kurt Cobain, but *Live Through This* (1994) established Hole as a musically serious entity in their own right. The album arrived just after Kurt's death, adding unavoidable biographical context to its already charged content. "There's nothing like success to spur imitation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Hole's second album, released four days after Kurt Cobain's death, achieved significant success. "Four days before her bandhole was to release their second album, Live Through This, Kurt died. Live Through This actually ended up doing very well."

podcast.body: In early April 1994, Courtney Love was in Los Angeles engaged in promotional activities for a new album by her band, Hole, when Kurt Cobain disappeared from rehab. "Courtney, who was in LA doing promotion for the new whole album, was freaked out by Kurt's disappearance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The album cover features a model named Lailani Bishop, portrayed as a beauty queen holding a bouquet of flowers. The concept, which Courtney Love conveyed to photographer Ellen Von Unwerth, was "miscongeniality" (as intended by the band). The band's logo on the album uses a font remarkably similar to that used by Mattel for Barbie dolls. "On the cover, we see what seems to be a beauty queen with a bouquet of flowers. The model's name is Lailani Bishop. The concept Courtney Lovegate to the photographer, whose name was Ellen Vaughan Unworth, was to come up with a misconjuniality theme."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Upon its release in April 1994, *Live Through This* became subject to widespread suspicions and accusations that Courtney Love received substantial songwriting assistance from her husband, Kurt Cobain. While it is considered reasonable for a musician couple to bounce ideas off each other, the extent of Cobain's alleged involvement became a contentious point for those skeptical of Love's authorship.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
